To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the next-to-leading QCD corrections are significant for the heavy-quark cross sections, and that the heavy-quark distributions in the virtual-photon frame can be used to probe the heavy quark production mechanism.

the next-to-leading-order corrections for heavy quark electroproduction are large, that they are dominated by soft-gluon emission, that the heavy quark production cross section is enhanced at small transverse momentum by the emission of soft gluons, that the heavy-quark transverse momentum distribution is sensitive to correlations with the heavy antiquark and the associated jet, and that the heavy quarks are preferentially produced in a jet.

We have completed the first next-to-leading order QCD calculations of the differential distributions for heavy quark pair production in deep-inlastic electron-proton scattering and have presented the first results for the associated jet structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of next-to-leading order QCD corrections to deep-inelastic electro-production of heavy quarks in the exclusive channel.
the calculation of next-to-leading order QCD corrections to heavy-quark production and heavy-quark correlations in electroproduction.
heavy quark production and correlations in deep-inelastice electroproduction at HERA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the next-to-leading corrections to the cross section are large (up to 100%) in the kinematic region of interest, but that the next-to-next-to-leading order corrections are expected to be small (of order 10% or less).
the heavy quark correlations are a very promising observable for the study of QCD at the HERA collider.
the heavy quark production cross sections are sensitive to higher-twist effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have completed all next-to-leading order calculations for heavy-quark correlations at HERA.
the heavy-quark correlation effects are small in the kinematical range of the HERA experiments, but they are not negligible.
the next-to-leading corrections to the heavy quark production cross section in deep inelastic scattering are large.
The main takeaway from our work is that
heavy quark correlations in the virtual-photon process are significantly different from those in the hadron process.
heavy-quark production at HERA will provide a very clean environment for the study of heavy-quark correlations and the associated dynamics.
the correlations among the heavy-quark, the heavy-antiquark and the associated jet are significant and should not be neglected.
